title: Declaration resolution and grouping of mentions
description:
Resolve each mention to its declaration and group data-item mentions by declaration. Decision 6 of the parent initiative.

## Scope

- Declaration resolution: local, parameter, class field, or function in the same file, or one hop through a relative import to the export. Reuse the scanner's relative-import resolution (`src/data-flow/import-graph.ts`). Package imports stay unresolved.
- Type annotation: when the declaration has a written type, record the type name and follow it one hop to its definition when it is in the repo. No inference.
- `payload.email` with `payload: SignupDto` resolves to the parameter and records `SignupDto`. It does not invent a declaration of `email`.
- Scan output gains a level: data item → declarations → mentions. The data item identity does not change.
- Import and assignment edges between declarations are recorded as a graph for later clustering.

## Done when

- In the labeled corpus scopes, email mentions collapse onto a declaration set, and each group's mentions share one declaration.
- An identifier imported from a relative module resolves to the export in that module.

## Evaluation

New grouping layer scored by pairwise precision and recall over mention pairs. Gold grouping follows the component consolidation rules in `tests/eval/canonical-representation.md`: group only on reviewed evidence; ambiguous grouping stays `needs_adjudication`.
